scenario: A cruise line records excursion bookings only for excursions with more than 150 seats sold. Revenue planners want the mean booking size across all excursions.

data.description: Only bookings above 150 seats are observed. Booking size is Normal with known sigma 40 seats.

question: Estimate (a) the true mean booking size mu across all excursions and (b) the fraction of excursions represented in the booking report.
naive_answer: Average excursion booking is about 169 seats because that is the report mean.
reasoning_trace: Alpha≈1.2 gives mu=150-1.2*40=102 and observed fraction about 0.1151.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(150-mu)/40; return mu+40*norm.pdf(a)/norm.sf(a)-169.49
mu=brentq(eq,-200,149.99)
frac=norm.sf((150-mu)/40)
assert abs(mu-102)<3 and abs(frac-0.1151)<0.005
